instruction: Hierarchical Sheet Split. `power.kicad_sch` is an abstract KiCad 10.0.2 power-connectivity fixture, not a manufacturer reference design. Each of its 95 symbols has a hidden `Section` property (`buck`, `ldo`, or `load`). The 78 source-defined two-terminal devices use real KiCad symbols and explicit `Net1`/`Net2` or diode `NetA`/`NetK` metadata; preserve their pin-to-net connectivity. The remaining 17 U/Q/J devices are explicitly marked `ConnectivityScope=unspecified_by_source`, use visible `Benchmark:*_Abstract` symbols, and have 58 intentional no-connect pins; do not infer or add electrical connections for them. Split the flat fixture into `buck.kicad_sch`, `ldo.kicad_sch`, and `load.kicad_sch` using each symbol's existing `Section` value. Preserve every reference, value, library ID, pin set, connectivity property, and inclusion flag, and place each reference in exactly one child without adding or removing components. Add boundary ports connected to the corresponding real child nets with these exact contracts: buck has `VBUCK` output and `GND` bidirectional; LDO has `VBUCK` input, `VLDO` output, and `GND` bidirectional; load has `VBUCK` input, `VLDO` input, and `GND` bidirectional. Create `/home/user/Desktop/top.kicad_sch` with exactly three sheet symbols referencing the sibling files. At the top level, wire all three `VBUCK` pins together, both `VLDO` pins together, and all three `GND` pins together, while keeping those three networks distinct. Layout and UUIDs may differ as long as the files are native KiCad 10.0.2 schematics and the hierarchy preserves the flat fixture's connectivity. Write `/home/user/Desktop/top.kicad_sch`, `/home/user/Desktop/buck.kicad_sch`, `/home/user/Desktop/ldo.kicad_sch`, and `/home/user/Desktop/load.kicad_sch`.
